best_for: Privacy-minded people with up to five devices who want a plain, open-source WireGuard VPN from Mozilla rather than a feature-packed one from a VPN brand.

points.title: What it costs
points.text: The annual plan works out to USD 4.99 per month, billed as USD 59.88 a year plus tax. Monthly billing is USD 9.99. First-time customers get a 30-day money-back guarantee. Prices were read on the date below.

points.title: Five devices, 30+ countries
points.text: One subscription covers up to 5 devices across Windows, macOS, Linux, Android and iOS. Mozilla lists more than 500 servers in over 30 countries and says it does not log, track or share network data.

points.title: Built on WireGuard
points.text: Connections use the WireGuard protocol. Extras include multi-hop routing through two locations, custom DNS and blocking of ads and ad trackers.

points.title: App exclusions, listed for three systems
points.text: Mozilla's features page lists excluding chosen apps from the VPN for Windows, Android and Linux. The Firefox extension that sets VPN rules per website is Windows only.

points.title: Open-source client
points.text: The app is MPL-2.0 and its code is public on GitHub. The Windows client supports Windows 10 and 11 on x64 and Windows 11 on Arm; the Windows installer listed here is machine-wide x64.

points.title: Linux from Mozilla
points.text: The Flatpak is published by Mozilla, and Flathub marks it verified, for x64 and Arm64. Mozilla also offers .deb and .rpm packages.

points.title: Versions kept here
points.text: The Windows listing keeps 63 versions. macOS and Linux list only the current release, so downgrades there need another source.
